2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 (now dead) as pre-emptor instituted the original Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case being No.03 of 2002 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Bahubal, Hobiganj contending inter alia that one Reaz Ullah was the owner of the case land under Khatian Nos.692 and 693. Reaz Ullah died leaving behind 03 (three) sons the opposite parties No.3-6 and 03 (three) daughters the opposite parties No.7-8 and one Kutubjan Nessa who died leaving behind 04 sons and 04 daughters. Reaz Ullah during his life time sold out 31 decimals of land under plot No.1323 of Khaitan No.692 in favour of one Bulbul Bibi on 30.07.1975. Reaz Ullah also sold out 21 decimals of land from plot No.1325 under khatian No.663 to one Abdul Ali and others on 30.07.1975. Subsequently; Abdul Ali and Bulbul Bibi sold out their purchased land in favour of the pre-emptor on 08.12.1977 and thus the pre-emptor became a co-sharer by purchase in the Case Jote. The further Case of the pre-emptor is such that he is also a contiguous land owner of the case land which is adjacent to plot No.1329. He purchased the land of plot No.1329 on 25.03.2001 and on 21.05.1984 by deed No.1651. One Omesh Chandra and Guno Moni were the owners of the land of 11 khatian No.678. Guno Moni died leaving behind one son Umesh Chandra Paul. Ebajot Ullah purchased 4 decimals of land from plot No.1341 of khaitan No.678 and by an amicable settlement between two brothers Abdur Razzak possessed that who is the brother of Ebajot Ullah. Subsequently; Abdur Razzak transferred the said land to the opposite party No.03 on 13.10.1988 and thereafter the opposite party Nos.3, 4 transferred their land in favour of the pre-emptees beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor on 04.11.2001 and for the said transfer no notice was served upon the pre-emptor. The pre-emptor for his necessity knowing about the Case Kabla filed the original pre-emption Miscellaneous Case for getting the case land pre-empted. 

 11. Having gone through the relevant law ' and the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties it appears that from Exhibits "ka" and "kha" which are the kahatians of the case land are 692 and 678. It was the case of the pre-emptor that in the deed the number of khatians were wrongly written as 590 and 591 instead of 692 & 693 and for the said reason he filed a suit being No.62 of 2007 in the court of learned Assistant judge, Bahubol and from Exhibit No.14 it appears that the aforesaid suit was decreed. It further appears that the appellate court scanning the documentary evidences rightly found that the pre-emptor is a contiguous land owner of the case land and is also a co-sharer by purchase in khatian No.692 and on this matter there is no controversy from the side of the pre-emptees. As to the eligibility or locus-standi of the pre-emptor there is no challenge from the side of the pre-emptee.
